items.name: zero arrow (via null object)
items.statement_summary: In a category with a null object z (both initial and terminal, recalled from §I.5), the zero arrow 0 = 0_b^a : a→b is the composite a→z→b of the unique arrows through z; any composite having a zero arrow as a factor is again zero, and the zero arrow is independent of the choice of null object.

items.name: kernel of an arrow
items.statement_summary: A kernel of f : a→b is an equalizer of the pair (f, 0 : a⇉b); equivalently a monic k : s→a with fk = 0 such that every h with fh = 0 factors uniquely as h = k h' through k.

items.name: kernels exist and are monic
items.statement_summary: Any category with a zero object and all equalizers (equivalently all pullbacks, or all finite limits) has a kernel for every arrow, unique up to isomorphism of the source; every kernel is monic (kg'=kh' implies g'=h') by the unique-factorization requirement, so a kernel may be viewed as a subobject of a.

items.name: cokernel of an arrow
items.statement_summary: The cokernel of f : a→b is the dual of the kernel (a coequalizer of f and 0): a universal epi u : b→q with uf = 0 through which every arrow annihilating f (post-composing to 0) factors uniquely; already described dually in §III.3.

items.name: in an Ab-category every equalizer is a kernel
items.statement_summary: In any Ab-category, for a parallel pair f,g : b→c an arrow h satisfies fh = gh iff (f−g)h = 0, so the equalizer of f,g coincides with the kernel of f−g; hence equalizers are kernels and one works with kernels rather than equalizers in R-Mod, Ab, etc.

items.name: ker/coker Galois connection between the preorders Q^c and P_c
items.statement_summary: For a category with zero, kernels and cokernels and an object c: P_c is the set of arrows into c preordered by g≤f iff g factors through f (restricting to monics gives the subobjects of c), and Q^c the set of arrows out of c preordered dually (u≥v iff v factors through u). Choosing a kernel for each u and cokernel for each f gives order maps ker : Q^c→P_c and coker : P_c→Q^c with f≤ker u ⇔ uf=0 ⇔ coker f≥u, forming a Galois connection (§IV.5) with triangular identities ker(coker(ker u))=ker u, coker(ker(coker f))=coker f, and g is a kernel iff g=ker(coker g).

items.name: canonical factorization f = mq with m = ker(coker f)
items.statement_summary: In any category with a null object, kernels and cokernels, every arrow f has a canonical factorization f = m q where m = ker(coker f).

items.name: diagonal fill-in for the canonical factorization; q epi
items.statement_summary: Given the canonical factorization f = mq (m = ker(coker f)) and any other factorization f = m'q' in which m' is a kernel, there is a unique diagonal arrow t with m = m't and q' = tq; moreover, if the category has equalizers and every monic is a kernel, then q is epi (so f = mq is an epi-mono factorization).

items.name: Ab-category
items.statement_summary: An Ab-category is a category in which each hom-set A(b,c) is a (not necessarily small) abelian group and composition is bilinear over this addition; the group's zero element is a zero arrow 0 : b→c (even absent a null object) and any composite with a zero arrow is zero. Recalled/restated from §I.8.

items.name: characterization of a null object in an Ab-category
items.statement_summary: For an object z of an Ab-category the following are equivalent: (i) z is initial; (ii) z is terminal; (iii) 1_z = 0 : z→z; (iv) A(z,z) is the zero group. In particular any initial or terminal object of an Ab-category is a null object.

items.name: the two zero arrows coincide
items.statement_summary: In an Ab-category with a null object z, the unique maps b→z and z→c are the zero elements of their hom-groups, and their composite b→z→c equals the zero element 0 of the abelian group A(b,c); i.e. the §1 zero morphism and the additive identity of the hom-group agree.

items.name: biproduct diagram
items.statement_summary: A biproduct diagram for objects a,b in an Ab-category is a⇄c⇄b with projections p1,p2 and injections i1,i2 satisfying p1 i1 = 1_a, p2 i2 = 1_b, and i1 p1 + i2 p2 = 1_c.

items.name: product iff biproduct iff coproduct in an Ab-category
items.statement_summary: In an Ab-category, two objects a,b have a product iff they have a biproduct iff they have a coproduct: given a biproduct diagram (c,p1,p2,i1,i2), the object c with p1,p2 is a product of a,b and dually c with i1,i2 is a coproduct; conversely a product diagram extends uniquely to a biproduct.

items.name: biproduct bifunctor ⊕ : A×A→A
items.statement_summary: When all binary biproducts exist, a chosen c = a⊕b for each pair makes ⊕ : A×A→A a bifunctor, with f1⊕f2 (for f1:a→a', f2:b→b') characterized equivalently by p'_j(f1⊕f2) = f_j p_j (as for the product ×) or by (f1⊕f2)i_k = i'_k f_k (as for the coproduct ⊔); the identification of the product bifunctor with the coproduct bifunctor is a natural isomorphism.

items.name: finite biproducts and the matrix calculus of arrows
items.statement_summary: Iterating yields finite biproducts ⊕_j a_j (j=1..n) characterized by i1 p1 + ... + in pn = 1 and p_k i_j = δ_{kj}; then A(⊕_k c_k, ⊕_j a_j) ≅ Σ_{j,k} A(c_k, a_j), each arrow f is determined by its n×m matrix of components f_{kj} = p_k f i_j, and composition of arrows is matrix multiplication of component matrices.

items.name: additive category
items.statement_summary: An additive category is an Ab-category having a zero object 0 and a biproduct for every pair of its objects.

items.name: addition of arrows recovered from the biproduct
items.statement_summary: In an additive category, for parallel arrows f,f' : a→b one has f + f' = δ^b (f⊕f') δ_a, where δ_a : a→a×a is the diagonal (p1δ_a = 1_a = p2δ_a) and δ^b : b⊔b→b the codiagonal (δ^b i1 = 1_b = δ^b i2); i.e. the additive structure is determined by the biproduct.

items.name: additive functor
items.statement_summary: An additive functor T : A→B between Ab-categories is a functor satisfying T(f+f') = Tf + Tf' for every parallel pair f,f'; consequently T0 = 0.

items.name: additive functor iff preserves biproducts
items.statement_summary: If A,B are Ab-categories and A has all binary biproducts, then a functor T : A→B is additive iff it carries every binary biproduct diagram in A to a biproduct diagram in B; equivalently iff it carries every binary product diagram to a product, equivalently iff it carries every binary coproduct diagram to a coproduct.

items.name: canonical map coproduct→product is iso
items.statement_summary: Show that in any additive category the canonical map κ : a1⊔...⊔an → a1×...×an (defined in §III.5) is an isomorphism; this is essentially a reformulation of Theorem 2.

items.name: infinite canonical map need not be iso
items.statement_summary: Define the canonical map κ from an infinite coproduct to the corresponding infinite product, and give an example showing it need not be an isomorphism in every additive category.

items.name: biproduct associative and commutative
items.statement_summary: Show that the biproduct in an additive category is associative and commutative up to a natural isomorphism.

items.name: alternative construction of addition of arrows
items.statement_summary: (a) For a category with a null object, finite products and finite coproducts in which the canonical map a1⊔a2→a1×a2 is always an isomorphism, define f+f' = δ^b(f×f')δ_a and prove each A(a,b) is a commutative monoid with composition distributive over it. (b) If additionally each object a has an arrow v_a : a→a with v_a + 1_a = 0, prove each A(a,b) is a group, so this addition gives A the structure of an additive category (Mac Lane 1950).

items.name: free Ab-category on a category C
items.statement_summary: Given a category C, construct an Ab-category A and a functor C→A universal from C to an Ab-category (hint: same objects as C, with A(b,c) = Z(C(b,c)) the free abelian group on the hom-set C(b,c)).

items.name: free additive category Add(A); Add(K)=Matr_K
items.statement_summary: (a) Given an Ab-category A, construct an additive category Add(A) and an additive functor A→Add(A) universal from A to an additive category (objects are n-tuples of A-objects, arrows are matrices of A-arrows). (b) For A the commutative ring K as a one-object Ab-category, show Add(K) is the category Matr_K of §I.2.

items.name: abelian category
items.statement_summary: An abelian category is an Ab-category satisfying: (i) it has a null object; (ii) it has binary biproducts; (iii) every arrow has a kernel and a cokernel; (iv) every monic arrow is a kernel and every epi is a cokernel.

items.name: abelian category has all finite limits and colimits
items.statement_summary: Conditions (i)-(ii) make an abelian category additive; a terminal or initial object may replace the null object (Prop VIII.2.1), and all products a×b or all binary coproducts may replace the biproducts. With (i)-(ii), the kernels of (iii) give all finite limits (the equalizer of f,g is ker(f−g); biproducts give finite products); dually cokernels give all finite colimits.

items.name: monic + epi implies iso in an abelian category
items.statement_summary: In an abelian category any arrow f : a→b that is both monic and epi is an isomorphism: f monic gives f = ker g for some g with gf = 0 = 0f, then f epi cancels to g = 0, and ker(0 : b→c) is equivalent to 1_b, so f is an isomorphism.

items.name: functor category A^J is abelian
items.statement_summary: R-Mod, Mod-R, Ab are abelian with the usual kernels/cokernels; and if A is abelian so is every functor category A^J: Nat(S,T) = A^J(S,T) is an abelian group under termwise addition ((α+β)_j = α_j + β_j), the functor constant at A's null object is the null functor, the biproduct S⊕T is (S⊕T)a = Sa⊕Ta termwise, and the kernel of a natural transformation α : S→T is (K j = ker α_j) termwise, so all axioms hold.

items.name: functorial monic-epi (image) factorization in an abelian category
items.statement_summary: In an abelian category every arrow f has a factorization f = m e with m monic and e epi, where m = ker(coker f) and e = coker(ker f). The factorization is functorial: for any other such factorization f' = m'e' and any morphism <g,h> : f→f' (a commutative square) there is a unique k with e'g = ke and m'k = hm; in particular any two monic-epi factorizations of f are isomorphic by a unique iso.

items.name: image and coimage of an arrow
items.statement_summary: For the monic-epi factorization f = m e : a→b, the image im f := m (a subobject of the codomain b) and the coimage coim f := e (a quotient object of the domain a), each determined up to isomorphism; more generally if f = m1 t e1 with m1 monic, t an isomorphism and e1 epi, then m1 ≡ im f, e1 ≡ coim f and t is the canonical coimage-to-image isomorphism.

items.name: exact at an object
items.statement_summary: A composable pair a→f b→g c is exact at b when im f = ker g as subobjects of b (equivalently coker f = coim g). Characterization: im f ≤ ker g iff gf = 0, and im f ≥ ker g iff every k with gk = 0 factors through m = im f; classically, gf = 0 and everything killed by g lies in the image of f.

items.name: short exact sequence
items.statement_summary: The diagram 0→a→f b→g c→0 (with 0 the null object) is a short exact sequence when it is exact at a, at b and at c; equivalently f is monic, g is epi, and f = ker g with g = coker f.

items.name: short right / short left exact sequence
items.statement_summary: Terminology introduced in prose: a sequence a→b→c→0 that is exact at b and at c (equivalently, h = coker f) is called a short right exact sequence; dually, a sequence 0→a→b→c exact at a and b (equivalently, k = ker f) is a short left exact sequence.

items.name: exact functor
items.statement_summary: A functor T:A→B between abelian categories is exact when it preserves all finite limits and all finite colimits; equivalently (since limits are built from products and equalizers) when T is additive and preserves kernels and cokernels, i.e. ker(Tf)=T(ker f) and coker(Tf)=T(coker f). An exact functor also preserves images and coimages and carries exact sequences to exact sequences.

items.name: left exact functor
items.statement_summary: A functor T is left exact when it preserves all finite limits; equivalently when T is additive and ker(Tf)=T(ker f) for every f; equivalently when T preserves short left exact sequences.

items.name: economical axiomatization of abelian categories (Freyd/Schubert)
items.statement_summary: Alternative characterization, stated with proof omitted (attributed to Freyd 1964 / Schubert 1970): a category satisfying the abelian-category axioms (i), (iii), (iv) together with (ii') existence of binary products and binary coproducts — rather than a given abelian-group structure on each hom-set — automatically admits an addition on each hom-set A(a,b) (via the formula (2.6)) making it an abelian category. The additive enrichment is derivable from finite (co)products.

items.name: exact iff preserves short exact sequences
items.statement_summary: Show that an additive functor T:A→B between abelian categories is exact iff it carries every short exact sequence in A to a short exact sequence in B.

items.name: product of abelian categories is abelian
items.statement_summary: Prove that if A and B are abelian categories then the product category A × B is abelian.

items.name: free abelian groups not abelian
items.statement_summary: Show that the category of all free abelian groups is not abelian.

items.name: finite abelian groups form an abelian category
items.statement_summary: Show that the category of all finite abelian groups (with all group morphisms as arrows) is abelian.

items.name: finitely generated modules over a left noetherian ring
items.statement_summary: If R is a left noetherian ring, show that the category of all finitely generated left R-modules (with all module morphisms) is abelian.

items.name: quotient object v/u; ker/im vs coim/coker duality
items.statement_summary: For subobjects u ≤ v of an object a in an abelian category, define a quotient object v/u agreeing with the usual notion in Ab; and if gf = 0, prove that ker g / im f is isomorphic to the dual object coim g / coker f.

items.name: chain complex
items.statement_summary: In an abelian category A, a chain complex is a sequence of composable arrows …→c_{n+1}→c_n→c_{n-1}→… with successive composites vanishing: ∂_n ∘ ∂_{n+1} = 0 for all n.

items.name: n-th homology object H_n c
items.statement_summary: For a chain complex, the n-th homology object measuring the deviation from exactness at c_n is H_n c = Ker(∂_n : c_n→c_{n-1}) / Im(∂_{n+1} : c_{n+1}→c_n); this definition works in any abelian category (the quotient as in Exercise VIII.3.6).

items.name: morphism of short exact sequences
items.statement_summary: A morphism ⟨m,e⟩→⟨m',e'⟩ of short exact sequences in A is a triple ⟨f,g,h⟩ of arrows making the two-row ladder diagram (3) (rows 0→a→b→c→0 and 0→a'→b'→c'→0, verticals f,g,h) commute.

items.name: category Ses A of short exact sequences
items.statement_summary: The short exact sequences of an abelian category A, together with their morphisms (triples ⟨f,g,h⟩), form a category Ses A, which is additive.

items.name: short five lemma
items.statement_summary: In any commutative diagram (3) of two short exact rows joined by a morphism ⟨f,g,h⟩: if f and h are monic then g is monic; and if f and h are epi then g is epi.

items.name: pullback of an epi is epi (abelian); kernel factorization
items.statement_summary: In an abelian category, given a pullback square with f:b→c epi and g:d→c, the pulled-back arrow f':s→d is epi; moreover the kernel k of f factors as k = g'k' where k' is the kernel of f'. (Pullbacks of monics are monic in any category, Lemma V.7; this supplies the epi case for abelian categories. In particular, pulling a short exact sequence a→b→c back along g:d→c yields a short exact sequence a→s→d.)

items.name: pullback of a short exact sequence; Ext(c,a) as a bifunctor
items.statement_summary: Given a short exact sequence a→b→c, any arrow g:d→c into the right-hand end yields by pullback a short exact sequence a→s→d; this operation and its dual (pushout) make Ext(c,a), the collection of short exact sequences from a to c, a bifunctor on an abelian category (reference: Mac Lane 1963, Chap. III). Ext itself is not developed here.

items.name: member of an object (x ∈_m a) and the relation ≡
items.statement_summary: A member x ∈_m a of an object a is any arrow with codomain a. Two members x,y of a are declared equivalent, x ≡ y, iff there exist epis u,v with xu = yv; this is an equivalence relation (transitivity uses Proposition 2), and a member is its ≡-class. Each object a has a zero member (class of the zero arrow 0→a) and each member x has a negative -x; every arrow f:a→b sends members of a to members of b respecting ≡. This apparatus supports element-free diagram chasing in any abelian category.

items.name: elementary rules for chasing diagrams with members
items.statement_summary: For members in any abelian category: (i) f:a→b is monic iff for all x ∈_m a, fx ≡ 0 implies x ≡ 0; (ii) f monic iff for all x,x' ∈_m a, fx ≡ fx' implies x ≡ x'; (iii) g:b→c is epi iff every z ∈_m c has some y ∈_m b with gy ≡ z; (iv) h:r→s is the zero arrow iff hx ≡ 0 for all x ∈_m r; (v) a→b→c is exact at b iff gf = 0 and every y ∈_m b with gy ≡ 0 has some x ∈_m a with fx ≡ y; (vi) (subtraction) if gx ≡ gy there is z ∈_m b with gz ≡ 0, and any f with fx ≡ 0 has fy ≡ fz while any h with hy ≡ 0 has hx ≡ -hz.

items.name: five lemma
items.statement_summary: In a commutative diagram (4) of two five-term rows with exact rows and vertical maps f_1,...,f_5: if f_1, f_2, f_4, f_5 are isomorphisms then f_3 is an isomorphism. (Proved by member chasing; by duality it suffices to show f_3 monic.)

items.name: induced kernel and cokernel rows of a morphism of short exact sequences
items.statement_summary: Given a morphism ⟨f,g,h⟩ of short exact sequences, adjoining the kernels (Kef, Keg, Keh) and cokernels (Cof, Cog, Coh) yields diagram (5) with exact columns; there are unique induced arrows m_0,e_0 forming a kernel row Kef→Keg→Keh and m_1,e_1 forming a cokernel row Cof→Cog→Coh making the added squares commute. A member chase shows the kernel row is exact at Kef and Keg, and the cokernel row is exact at Cog and Coh; the kernel row need not be short exact — e_0 need not be epi, failing precisely when m_1 is not monic.

items.name: snake lemma (ker-coker sequence)
items.statement_summary: Given a morphism ⟨f,g,h⟩ of short exact sequences (diagram (3)), there is a connecting arrow δ : Keh→Cof making the six-term ker-coker sequence 0→Kef→Keg→Keh→(δ)→Cof→Cog→Coh→0 exact. δ is constructed from a pullback (of e and ker h) and a pushout (of coker f and m'), with the usual zig-zag description on members; full exactness is proved by member chasing.

items.name: minimal hypotheses for f_3 monic in the five lemma
items.statement_summary: In the five lemma, obtain minimal hypotheses on f_1, f_2, and f_4 only for f_3 to be monic.

items.name: five lemma f_3 epi via members
items.statement_summary: In the five lemma, prove f_3 epi using members (not comembers); the hint notes Rule (vi) of Theorem 3 is necessary in this proof.

items.name: complete exactness of the ker-coker sequence
items.statement_summary: Complete the proof of the exactness of the ker-coker (snake) sequence.

items.name: connecting morphism δ is natural
items.statement_summary: Show that the connecting morphism δ is natural: a natural transformation between two appropriate functors defined on a suitable category whose objects are morphisms (3) of short exact sequences.

items.name: 3x3 lemma and middle 3x3 lemma
items.statement_summary: For a bordered-by-zeros commutative 3x3 diagram: (a) give a direct proof of the 3x3 lemma — if all three columns and the last two rows are short exact, then so is the first row; (b) show this also follows from the ker-coker sequence; (c) prove the middle 3x3 lemma — if all three columns and the first and third rows are short exact, then so is the middle row.

items.name: six-term exact sequence for a composite gf
items.statement_summary: For arrows f:a→b and g:b→c, establish the exact sequence 0→Kef→Ke(gf)→Keg→Cof→Co(gf)→Cog→0.

items.name: Ses(A) not abelian in general
items.statement_summary: Show explicitly that the category Ses(A) of short exact sequences is not in general abelian.

items.name: Lubkin-Haron-Freyd-Mitchell embedding theorem
items.statement_summary: Stated (in the chapter Notes, without proof) as an alternative route to the diagram lemmas: for any small abelian category A there exist a faithful exact functor A→Ab and a full and faithful exact functor A→R-Mod for a suitable ring R (Lubkin-Haron-Freyd-Mitchell embedding theorems). Consequently the abelian-category diagram lemmas can be reduced to the case of R-modules.
